diseases.name: Cherry Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal disease of cherry leaves that causes spotting, yellowing and early leaf fall.
diseases.causes: Spores from last year's fallen leaves are splashed onto young leaves in wet spring and summer weather.
symptoms: Small purple to red-brown spots on the upper leaf
White to pink spore masses under the spots in wet weather
Spotted leaves turn yellow and drop
diseases.effect: Trees lose many leaves by midsummer, so fruit ripens poorly.
diseases.untreated: Repeated early leaf loss weakens trees and makes them prone to winter injury.

steps.title: Clear fallen leaves
steps.instruction: Rake up and remove or bury fallen leaves in autumn.
steps.rationale: The fungus overwinters in the leaf litter.

steps.title: Open up the canopy
steps.instruction: Prune so leaves dry quickly after rain.
steps.rationale: Spores need wet leaves to infect.

steps.title: Protective fungicide from petal fall
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product on the label's schedule while wet weather lasts.
steps.rationale: Protects new leaves through the infection period.

prevention.title: Check leaves after spring rain
prevention.detail: Early spots mean the season's infections have started.

lifecycle: The fungus overwinters in fallen leaves.
Spring rain splashes spores onto young leaves.
Purple spots appear; spores form underneath.
Leaves yellow and drop, and new spores spread.
conditions: Fallen leaves left under the tree.
